original_card.question: Can a changed G20 helper path or independent-target split improve the complete BIT moment without losing its physical endpoint?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A full boundary contract and paid profile; unchanged scalar counts alone are insufficient. A scoped local result may be retained without a complete supplier. Expanding it into further construction rounds requires the family-level budget and obligation gate in research-family-status.md; an optimistic passing relaxation alone is not acceptance.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: First read #5679/#5708 and their audits as pending component proposals. Choose one uncovered helper group/cut on an exact word; compare arbitrary-input native action, targets, owned storage, both orientations and full signed bill. Stop if the gain is only a scalar count or repaid by lost targets. Do not rerun the frozen #5609 common-frame domain without changing its hypothesis.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.
allowed_variations: One exact source head, helper/cut region or quantified proposition and changed hypothesis; check live handoffs first. Different seeds are not different scopes.
scope_change_triggers: Changing source head, helper/cut domain, operation alphabet or caller boundary without recording the new scope.
Treating an archived proposal or local numerical pass as complete supplier admission.

existing_checks.scope: Selected PR5599: complete helper-subspace construction and independent caller replay; five framework assumptions remain.
existing_checks.remaining: The next experiment must identify uncovered source-specific work. Successor archive intake does not transfer this admission.

actual_scope: Prove that the n - v + z unit-ADD floor of a target data block holds for every word on any number of added wires, whatever their initial or final contract, and apply it to the pinned PR5840 G20 boundary: no scratch wire, external wire or tariff lowers a legal GL(2)-commutant side below 38 unit ADDs.
scope_change_reason: The card asks for a changed G20 helper path or target split. PR6641 leaves a narrower live question on the same boundary: whether one priced scratch wire, or a gate that leaves the 32 wires, lowers the 38-ADD side. That question is answered here for every number of extra wires. Helpers, targets and the recursive moment are unchanged.
bottleneck_link: A cheaper boundary word would lower the scalar BIT conversion invoice. Workspace was the remaining unpriced route left by the scratch-free floors. It is closed for unit binary ADD words, so a BIT improvement on this boundary must change the target, the controller or the gate alphabet.
stop_rule: Stop when the extended-wire floor is proved and bound to the pinned boundary. Do not search for nonlinear gates or changed output placements.
evidence: PROOF in README.md; verify.py replays both pinned sides, eight extended-wire controls, a step-by-step potential check on 400 seeded random words with extra wires, and every state of GL(4, F2) against every data-wire subset.
author: Nick Petalas
ai_assistance: Independent human and formal proof-kernel review are unclaimed.

open_questions.question: Can a word that leaves the data on a different set of physical wires, charged for the consumer's relabelling, beat 76 ADDs per port?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The floor fixes the 32 output labels. Ending a side on scratch wires and relabelling the consumer is a different contract that this proof does not cover.
open_questions.first_step: Price the consumer-side relabel and compute n - v + z for the row-permuted data block of one side.
open_questions.blocked_by: Requires a caller contract that accepts relocated outputs.

open_questions.question: Does a nonlinear or non-unit gate (Toffoli, carry, multi-target XOR at one unit) lower either side?
open_questions.why_it_matters: The potential argument uses only two-wire XOR gates. A multi-target or controlled gate changes the alphabet and the bound.
open_questions.first_step: Fix one priced multi-target XOR tariff and redo the potential count on the four-wire exchange corner.
open_questions.blocked_by: No such gate is priced in the current native model.
